page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor features a large 260 MB L3 cache alongside 2 MB L2 and 48 KB L1d caches. It lacks local storage and bundled GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching 34.94 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving a top-tier result of 15.23 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 8880.74 and a PassMark CPU score of 15831.29. Memory bandwidth is measured at 61.58 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 35.51 GB/sec for write operations. The instance demonstrates capable performance in small-scale AI workloads, processing 348.78 tokens/sec for text generation with a 135M parameter model, though performance drops significantly to 7.17 tokens/sec when generating text with a larger 7B parameter model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-highcpu-8 offers a dense compute-to-RAM ratio of 1:2, making it a resource-efficient choice for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The inclusion of Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) provides hardware acceleration for cryptography and vector calculations without the cost of a dedicated GPU. This instance is well-suited for compute-heavy tasks such as single-threaded data compression, web serving, lightweight machine learning inference, and general-purpose batch processing.
